ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Doppler radar utilizes the Doppler effect for tasks such as positioning, velocity measurement, and ranging. The Doppler effect refers to the phenomenon where the frequency of vibrations received by an observer differs from the frequency emitted by the vibration source when there is relative motion between the source of vibrations (such as sound, light, and radio waves) and the observer. Both the sound source $S$ and the observer A are moving in the positive direction of the $x$-axis, with velocities relative to the ground being $v_{s}$ and $v_{A}$, respectively. The speed of sound propagation in air is $v_{p}$, and it is assumed that $v_{s} < v_{p}$ and $v_{A} < v_{p}$, with no air flow relative to the ground.

1. If a sound source emits two sound signals in succession with a time interval of $\Delta t$, determine the time interval $\Delta t^{\prime}$ between the reception of these two sound signals by an observer based on the propagation process of these signals from the source to the observer.
2. Using the result from (1), derive the relationship between the frequency of the sound wave received by the observer and the frequency of the sound wave emitted by the source in this scenario.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the attached figure there is a horizontal x-axis, with the positive direction pointing to the right; the sound source S is located on the left side, and the observer A is located on the right side. Above S is marked an arrow of velocity v_s, and above A is marked an arrow of velocity v_A; both arrows point to the right, indicating that both the sound source and the observer move along the positive direction of the x-axis, and the initial position may be taken as S being to the left of A. Then reason: According to the diagram, take the sound source S to be at x=0 and the observer A to be at x=L when t=0. Suppose the times at which the sound source emits two signals are respectively t_1=0 and t_2=Δt; the times at which the first and second signals are received by A are respectively T_1 and T_2, therefore the receiving time interval is Δt'=T_2-T_1. First signal: It is emitted from x=0 and propagates to the right at sound speed v_p; when it is received, the observer's position is L+v_A T_1. Therefore there is v_p T_1 = L + v_A T_1, that is, (v_p-v_A)T_1=L. Second signal: The emission time is Δt, and at this time the sound source's position is v_s Δt; the propagation time of this signal is T_2-Δt, and when it is received the observer's position is L+v_A T_2. Therefore there is v_s Δt + v_p(T_2-Δt)=L+v_A T_2. After rearranging, (v_p-v_A)T_2=L+(v_p-v_s)Δt. Subtract the first equation from the second equation to eliminate L: (v_p-v_A)(T_2-T_1)=(v_p-v_s)Δt. Because Δt'=T_2-T_1, Δt' = [(v_p-v_s)/(v_p-v_A)] Δt. If the period emitted by the sound source is Δt, then f=1/Δt; the period received by the observer is Δt', then f'=1/Δt'. Therefore f'/f = Δt/Δt' = (v_p-v_A)/(v_p-v_s), so f' = [(v_p-v_A)/(v_p-v_s)] f.
